title: Meridian Infrastructure Group Legal Services Panel 2027
description: Three-year legal services panel for corporate, infrastructure and construction, disputes and regulatory work across the group's UK operations.
intro: Meridian Infrastructure Group owns and operates regulated water, rail depot and energy infrastructure assets across the United Kingdom. The group is appointing a panel of law firms for a three-year term covering corporate, infrastructure and construction, disputes and regulatory work.
This invitation to tender (ITT-2027-LEGAL-03) invites qualified firms to respond. All information in this document is confidential to the group and the invited firms.

sections.title: Introduction and Background
intro: The group spends approximately 2.4 million pounds per year on external legal services. The panel replaces the current arrangements which expire on 31 March 2027.
This section sets out the background to the appointment. Detailed requirements follow in sections 3 to 12.

items.text: Firms must acknowledge receipt of this invitation by email to panel@meridian-infra.example within three business days.

sections.title: Submission Instructions
intro: The following instructions apply to all responses. The group reserves the right to reject non-compliant responses without evaluation.

items.text: Responses must be submitted electronically via the group procurement portal no later than 12 February 2027, 12:00 UTC.
The response shall not exceed 40 pages, excluding CVs and the pricing schedule.
Firms must complete the Pricing Schedule (Attachment B) in the format provided.
Firms must attach a copy of their professional indemnity insurance certificate (Attachment C).
Clarification questions must be submitted in writing by 12 January 2027; answers will be shared with all firms.
Tenders must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

sections.title: Firm Information
intro: This section concerns the firm's background, standing and structure.

items.text: Provide an overview of the firm, including the year of establishment, number of partners and total fee earners.
List the offices from which panel work would be delivered.
Describe the firm's financial standing, including turnover for the last financial year and the availability of audited accounts.
State the regulatory body that regulates the firm and any quality accreditations held (for example Lexcel).
Confirm whether the firm has an office in Singapore or Dubai.
items.note: Trap: the firm has UK offices and European alliance firms only.

items.text: Describe the firm's ownership structure.

sections.title: Practice Expertise
intro: This section concerns the depth of expertise in the practice areas covered by the panel.

items.text: Describe your corporate and mergers and acquisitions capability, including the number and aggregate value of transactions completed in the last three years.
Describe your experience of infrastructure and construction projects under NEC4 and JCT contract forms.
Describe your public procurement expertise, including advice under the Procurement Act 2023.
Describe your construction disputes capability, including adjudication and Technology and Construction Court proceedings, with the number of adjudications handled in the last 24 months.
Describe your international arbitration experience, including ICC and LCIA arbitrations.
Confirm whether the firm holds a Band 1 ranking in Chambers UK for Tax.
items.note: Trap: no directory ranking evidence for tax.

items.text: Confirm whether the firm advises on Scots law matters from its Edinburgh office.
items.note: Trap: no Scots-law qualified capability is documented.

items.text: The firm must be able to advise on planning and environmental consents for linear infrastructure.

sections.title: Proposed Team
intro: This section concerns the individuals who would deliver panel work.

items.text: Identify the proposed relationship partner and summarise their relevant experience.
Identify the lead partners for construction and for disputes work, with their years of post-qualification experience.
Describe the partner-to-associate leverage you propose for panel matters.
Describe how you will ensure continuity of the named team and the notice you will give of any changes.
Describe your approach to supervision of junior lawyers working on panel matters.
Confirm whether a Welsh-speaking partner is available for matters in Wales.
items.note: Trap: no Welsh-language capability is documented.

sections.title: Relevant Experience
intro: This section concerns recent matters comparable to the group's work. Client names are only expected where disclosure is permitted.

items.text: Provide two examples of comparable-scale infrastructure matters completed in the last three years.
Describe a construction dispute you have resolved through adjudication, including the outcome.
Describe your experience of rail depot or rolling stock programmes.
Provide referee contact details for two clients whom the group can contact.
Describe your track record advising energy utilities.
Confirm whether the firm has acted on a PFI hospital project in the last three years.
items.note: Trap: no healthcare PFI matter exists.

sections.title: Service Delivery
intro: This section concerns how the firm manages the relationship day to day.

items.text: State your standard response times for acknowledging and substantively responding to instructions.
Describe your reporting arrangements, including the frequency of matter reports and panel review meetings.
Describe the key performance indicators you propose for the panel and how they will be measured.
Describe any secondment arrangements offered to panel clients.
Describe the training and know-how you will provide at no additional charge.
Describe your complaints handling procedure.
Confirm whether you provide a dedicated 24x7 helpdesk staffed by qualified solicitors.
items.note: Trap: an out-of-hours partner line exists, not a 24x7 helpdesk.

sections.title: Fees and Value
intro: This section concerns rates, fee arrangements and billing. The Pricing Schedule (Attachment B) is scored separately.

items.text: Provide your proposed hourly rates by grade of fee earner.
State the discount offered against standard rates for panel work.
Describe the alternative fee arrangements you offer, including fixed and capped fees.
Describe your billing arrangements, including e-billing capability and invoice format.
Describe how you provide and manage matter budgets and estimates, including notification before an estimate is exceeded.
Confirm whether the firm accepts payment of fees in Bitcoin or other cryptocurrency.
items.note: Trap: no payment-method evidence beyond bank transfer.

items.text: State your policy on disbursements and any mark-up applied.

sections.title: Risk, Insurance and Data Security
intro: This section concerns the protection of the group's information and the firm's regulatory standing.

items.text: State the level of professional indemnity insurance cover held and the insurer's rating.
Describe your information security controls and any certifications such as ISO 27001.
Describe your compliance with UK GDPR and where client data is hosted.
Describe your business continuity arrangements and recovery time objectives.
Describe your anti-money laundering and sanctions screening procedures.
The firm must disclose any professional negligence claims or regulatory findings against it in the last five years.
Confirm whether the firm holds Cyber Essentials Plus certification.
items.note: Trap: the firm holds Cyber Essentials, not Plus.

items.text: Confirm whether the firm holds ISO 14001 environmental certification.

sections.title: Technology and Innovation
intro: This section concerns the tools and methods the firm uses to deliver work efficiently.

items.text: Describe your matter management and client extranet capabilities.
Describe your use of document automation for standard documents.
Describe your policy on the use of generative AI tools and how client confidentiality is protected.
Describe your legal project management capability.
Confirm whether the firm is a licensed Alternative Business Structure (ABS).

sections.title: Diversity, ESG and Pro Bono
intro: This section concerns the firm's people, environmental and community commitments.

items.text: Provide the firm's diversity data, including the percentage of female partners.
Describe the firm's environmental commitments, including any net zero target.
State the number of pro bono hours delivered in the last year.
Describe your wellbeing initiatives for staff.
Confirm whether the firm holds the Living Wage Foundation accreditation.

sections.title: Conflicts and Contractual Terms
intro: This section concerns conflicts of interest and the contractual basis of the appointment.

items.text: Describe your conflict-check process, including turnaround time and the use of information barriers.
The firm must accept a liability cap of not less than 50 million pounds per claim.
State the notice period you require for termination of the framework.
State your standard payment terms.
Describe your position on client audit rights and on subcontracting of panel work.
